title: Flashing Lights
essence: A silent scream: a scream whose rings travel inward. The man floats in black while walls cave on him, wakes after midnight to a phone that rings twice and a mirror that answers his hand exactly, then his pupil opens and we go through it into a winter living room where he is six, a dead seven-year-old stands one pencil notch taller, his parents argue in a car with its hazards flashing, and he throws the tambourine she gave him through the glass.
palette_notes: The district is The Overseer: deep indigo night and electric blue from 18a6390f (blue skyline over black water, red beacon streaks) and ec036b41 (moon in a ring of towers). The flashing lights are three colours only: headlight white (#e8edf5), hazard amber (#f0a830) and the red beacon of 3603f621 (#d8322e). #7f97b8 is the ghost child's grey-blue wash. #5aa7ff is the suite accent, given here to the phone glow and the far light at the end of the road.

full_text.line: I heard a scream for help while falling with my headlights off.
It was a type of silent scream a trap lover makes to escape a pending marriage,
a concussion, a set of walls caving inward, seething and simmering,
and a solitude of crowds and smiles.
I received an emergency call while tossing and turning.
It was a type of silent call a man makes to the mirror after midnight.
To digest the truth, a windless insomnia and epiphany of a road winding down.
After a day of life dilated at the sun as long and as wise as possible, we won't make it.
I was six I recall when the ghost of a dead and loveless seven-year-old child appeared
and shared that my parents marriage wouldn't last.
It was a type of warm and heavy breeze in winter
where a child is left home alone.
With curtains pulled and blinds up as far and as wise as possible to see flashing lights
and the whispering screams of two souls on a road winding down.
And no tears and no fucks, no love to give, old to teach.

insights: Everything in this world collapses inward: rings, dark, sound. Animate every radiating thing backwards and the poem's grammar is done for you.
Size the two children to the door post, not to each other: one notch is the difference between the living and the dead.
Rooms here are filled dark fields with holes cut in them; the holes (mirror, bed, window) are the only lit paper. Outlined rooms on cream read as diagrams.
The mirror is free: build POET's half and flip it on the centre line so the hands meet exactly.
Three light colours only (white, amber, red) and never mixed in one sweep, or flashing becomes disco.
The tambourine must leave whole: its breaking belongs to 03.
Atlas: the Overseer is symmetry: put the moon exactly on the axis between two towers and the child exactly centred in the window. Any off-centre composition loses the sense of being watched.
Atlas: no salt line and no ceramic plates on the hill; a clean wall is honest here. Do not carry the 01/03 dressing into this street.
Atlas: sets/5e0fe00a4402b2bb-1 (boy from behind, blue window, sedan at the curb) is the master shot of the poem; build the living-room card stack to reproduce it.
future: The tambourine, whole, flies into 03's chapel through the rose window and shatters there; its pieces are 04's trail.
The living-room window and the woman as MOTHER return in 09.
The black void continues as 03's opening.

atlas.district_language: Two districts. The Black (02.0-02.1) again: no geography, no flood line, no seam; a black stage where the only light is strobing practicals and the figure lit alone, so build nothing behind him but black velvet card and let flash gels do the work. The Overseer (02.2-02.5) is watched, cold and symmetrical: after midnight in winter, one-point perspective with the moon dead on the axis between two slab towers, as if the moon were a lamp hung over the street. Paint the whole outside in five blues (#091a38 to #3d6a9a, accent #1078da) with no street lamps on the towers' side: moonlight, screen-blue, one crimson beacon high on a tower and the car's headlights and amber hazards are the only warm things. Towers are flat slab cards with blue pipework and tiny lit windows punched and backed with blue gel; the roofless palace sits on the ridge as a silhouette. The house is a brick rowhouse with a marble stoop and a big street-facing ground-floor window. The hill is under no line: do not draw a salt line or ceramic plates here; a clean wall is honest in this district. Inside the room keep it dark with one warm lamp so the window is a cold blue screen the child stands against in silhouette.

staging.name: Falling with headlights off
staging.shot: Floating wide on a black stage. POET card mid-frame on a slow drift rig, EX card back-to-camera lower right at a fixed distance on the same rig so the gap never changes. Strobe gels (white, then amber hazard) flash across both; a ring of small warm floor-lights below them like the drowned cathedral's lamps. Wall cards slide in from the edges and cave inward.

staging.name: Eyes dilate
staging.shot: Extreme close-up: the eye card fills frame; the iris is 3 concentric ring cards that iris open (pupil hole widens). Push straight through the pupil; behind it the night road winding down with two headlight beams fanning, which becomes the street of the next scene.

staging.name: Car pulls up
staging.shot: From behind YOUNG_POET at child height: his black silhouette card centre-low, the window a big backlit blue screen with cross mullions; outside, the rowhouse street, palace and towers under the moon. The car silhouette slides in along the curb; two headlight beam cards (soft-edged yellow acetate) sweep across ceiling and wall twice as it takes the bumps.

staging.name: The ghost child
staging.shot: Two-shot at child height beside the window: GHOST_CHILD a pale outline card lit from behind, one notch taller than YOUNG_POET, hugs him (arm card overlaps). Insert: frost-breath card fogging on the pane, his breath not the boy's. The ghost fades by swapping to thinner outline cards.

staging.name: Parents arguing in the car
staging.shot: Over the child's shoulder through the glass to the lit car: interior a warm cut-out window in the car silhouette with two small parent profiles (MOTHER passenger, father driver), amber hazards blinking. Behind the car, the moon exactly on the axis between two slab towers. Reverse: the child's face card in headlight wash, blinds up, curtain pulled aside.

staging.name: Tambourine through the window
staging.shot: From outside looking in: the window card face-on, the room a warm box behind it, the child small inside. The pane is a pre-scored sheet that swaps to a shards card; the tambourine card flies toward the lens on a rod, jingles flicking, and keeps going into black (the flight that lands in 03).

heroes.name: The Child's House
heroes.in_poem: every Overseer scene: the ground-floor window over the curb, the room behind it, the car at the curb
heroes.build_as_cards: Exterior: a brick rowhouse front card, marble stoop as two pale step strips, the big ground-floor window cut out with real acetate behind (pre-scored for the break). Interior: a shallow box: back wall with door post and pencil notches, lamp, sofa card, and the window wall in front. The window glass is the one thing that breaks; build three panes and a shard card.

heroes.build_as_cards: A reusable rowhouse facade kit: brick card in the blue night grade, marble stoop strips, sash window cut-outs and a cornice strip; reverse side painted warm for daylight poems.

transitions.how: In from 01 by a push through the pupil: the black continues from the hole in the party floor, the eye card fills frame and its pupil opens onto the night road.

One tracking object, no people: the tambourine leaves the shattered window toward the lens, flies through black, and enters the chapel's lancet window in 03. Build it on a long rod across a black belt so the same card crosses both sets.
